hints: Try the identity permutation for the first array.
A block of consecutive values can be paired in reverse order so each pair has the same sum.
Choose a prime just larger than the current largest unused value to form such a block.
analogy: A prime sum acts like a mirror: each value i pairs with prime-i.
example: For n=3, prime 5 pairs 2 with 3 and 3 with 2; the remaining 1 pairs with itself to sum to 2.
algorithm: Sieve primes through 2n. Set a[i]=i. While the largest unused value is r, choose the smallest prime p greater than r and set l=p-r. For i from l through r set b[i]=p-i, then continue with r=l-1. Print both permutations.
correctness: Bertrand's postulate ensures a prime between r and 2r for r>1, so l is positive and at most r; r=1 uses p=2. Each block maps onto itself by reversal, so b is a permutation and every pair sums to p.
complexity: For n values, O(n log log n) sieve time and O(n) space.
